tldr: Prime Intellect launched Prime Inference on Oct 8 as a hosted serving option for frontier open models. On Oct 21 the vLLM blog introduced Humming, a quantized-inference kernel library from Ant Group and the vLLM community.
whats_new: Resin, a native scheduler for LLM inference engines, appeared as a Show HN on Oct 26, extending the speed push from hosted serving and kernels to scheduling.
why_it_matters: Inference speed work is now landing at three layers (hosted serving, kernels, scheduling), so latency gains can come from swapping a layer instead of changing models.

beats.headline: Prime Inference offers fast serving for frontier open models
Humming brings quantized kernels to vLLM
beats.summary: Ant Group and the vLLM community report broad GPU and quantization support with vLLM integration.

open_questions: Does Resin publish benchmarks against existing engine schedulers?
Which inference engines does Resin support beyond the initial release?
take_for_builders: Benchmark Humming on your own quantized models and GPUs before adopting it, and treat Resin as an experiment until it publishes comparisons.
